Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a classic azygos lobe in the right upper zone, characterized by the azygos fissure and the inverted comma-shaped azygos vein. In standard radiological classifications of this variant, Type A is defined by the trigonum parietale (the pleural reflection at the base of the fissure) being located in the lateral aspect of the pulmonary apex, which corresponds to the typical appearance seen here.
